short.en: A plan for every rupee before you spend it.
Things you must have: food, school, bus fare, medicine.
Things that make life nicer but can wait: snacks, games, new clothes.
A box or pot at home for saving coins. Safe from spending, not from rats or thieves.
Prices going up over time. In this game, about 6% a year.
The price of money. You earn it when you save. You pay it when you borrow.
Interest only on the amount you started with.
Interest on interest. Great for savings, dangerous for debts.
A bank account for a child, opened with a parent or guardian. Many have zero minimum balance.
A government zero-balance bank account, with a RuPay card and accident cover.
A village banking agent who opens accounts and handles deposits for a bank.
The shop's notebook of what you owe. Easy to start, easy to forget, never forgets you.
One-time password sent by SMS. It is a key to your money. Never share it.
Your secret number for UPI or ATM. Only needed to send money, never to receive it.
A way to send money from your phone using a UPI ID or QR code.
A UPI request asking YOU to pay. Entering your PIN sends money away.
A square code you scan to pay. Scanning to "receive" money is a common trick.
Equated monthly instalment: the same payment every month until a loan is paid off.
A shop loan split into EMIs. Often has fees and high late charges.
A one-time charge for giving you a loan. Add it to the real cost.
The best thing you give up when you choose something else.
An app where you bet money on games or matches. The app wins over time. Many are illegal.
A bank loan for study. Repayment usually starts after the course ends.
Good debt helps you earn more later. Bad debt pays for things that lose value.
Industrial Training Institute: 1–2 year government skill courses, like electrician or fitter.
A paper showing your pay, what was added and what was cut, each month.
Retirement savings: 12% of your basic pay, matched by your employer.
A 10-character tax ID. Needed for bank accounts, salaries and big purchases.
Tax on earnings above a yearly limit. Most first jobs fall below it.
3–6 months of expenses kept safe and easy to reach.
A private lender. Fast and easy, but usually very costly, and often in rates per month.
Phone apps that lend in minutes. Many charge huge fees; illegal ones harass borrowers.
Borrowing for a month free. Pay only the minimum and interest runs at 36–42% a year.
A number from 300 to 900 showing how well you repay. Banks check it before lending.
10–20 women who save together each month and lend to members at low interest.
A loan against your gold jewellery. Cheaper than a sahukar, but you can lose the gold.
A low-interest bank loan for farming costs, about 7% a year, less if repaid on time.
A government-backed bank loan for small businesses, without collateral.
Someone whose bank account is used to move stolen money. It is a crime, even for "commission".
The national cyber-crime helpline. Call 1930 fast if you are cheated online.
You pay a small fixed amount. If something bad happens, the insurer pays the big bill.
The amount you pay for insurance, monthly or yearly.
Pure life cover for a fixed period. Low premium, big cover, no money back.
Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana: ₹2 lakh accident cover for ₹20 a year.
Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana: ₹2 lakh life cover for ₹436 a year.
Free hospital cover up to ₹5 lakh a year for eligible families.
Telangana's free health scheme for eligible families at listed hospitals.
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana: farmers pay about 2% of cover; pays out when crops fail.
₹6,000 a year from the government to farmers who own land, in three parts.
Money locked in a bank for a fixed time at a fixed rate, about 6–7% a year.
Save the same amount in the bank every month at a fixed rate.
A 15-year government savings scheme, about 7% a year, tax-free.
A government savings scheme for a girl child's future, with a good fixed rate.
Systematic investment plan: putting a fixed amount into a fund every month.
A low-cost fund that buys a little of many big companies. It swings, but spreads risk.
Not keeping all your eggs in one basket. Spread money across different things.
What a seller earns for selling you something. Bigger commission, bigger push.
A policy that mixes cover and savings. Usually low cover, high fees, long lock-in.
A group pools money monthly; each month one member takes the pot. Use only registered chits.
A fake scheme that pays old members with new members' money, until it collapses.
Fake police on a video call demanding money. Real police never arrest over a call.
Moving cash outside banks, without records. Illegal, and carriers get caught first.
The official record of who owns and farms a piece of land.
A paper from the registration office showing if land is already sold, mortgaged or disputed.
The registered paper that transfers land from seller to buyer.
The part of a big purchase you pay yourself. The rest is the loan.
A government pension scheme: ₹1,000–₹5,000 a month from age 60, for small monthly payments.
A long-term government-run pension account. You choose how much to add.
The person who receives your account or policy money if something happens to you.
Know Your Customer: ID papers the bank keeps. Update it at the branch, never through a link.
Telangana's marriage help scheme for eligible families, paid to the bride's mother.
Everything you own minus everything you owe.
